newsitem.title: GERMANY: German trade with East Europe rose 9.6 pct in H1.
newsitem.headline: German trade with East Europe rose 9.6 pct in H1.

text.p: German trade with central and eastern Europe rose to 62.8 billion marks in the first half of 1996, up 9.6 percent from the year-earlier half, the economics ministry reported on Monday.
Germany's overall world trade grew only 2.3 percent in the same period, the ministry said.
German exports to the central and eastern European states, including the former Soviet republics, jumped 15.1 percent to 33.3 billion marks, while imports rose 3.9 percent to 30 billion marks.
Poland was Germany's largest trading partner in the region, accounting for total trade of 13.3 billion marks, followed by Russia with 12.3 billion marks.
